In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
compartment models are only reliable when the permeability of the capillaries is high and interstitial volume is small, which is the case for most tissues.
the compartment model can be used as an approximation for capillary permeability and intercapillary distance, but it is not suitable for estimating the interstitial volume fraction.
the permeability-limtied compartment model yields reliable values only in a very narrow range of parameter values, which is unlikely to be encountered in practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the permeability-limted one-compartment model should be used with caution for estimating capillary permeability and interstitual volume fraction in DSC-MRI, especially for small capillary permeabilities.
the permeability-limted one-compartment model should be used with caution and only if the intercapillary distance is <100 μm and the vessel radius >10 μm.
the permeability-limitted compartment model is not suitable for capillaries of a radius of 3.3-4 μm, but it is suitable for larger capillaries.

compartment models should be used with great caution in estimating capillary permeability and interstitual volume fraction, especially in the case of capillaries with small radii.
compartment models can only be applied to estimate vascular parameters if they are not too large, i.e., the capillary radius should not exceed 4 μm.
